comparator.name: Spanish Language and Culture (Spaanse Taal en Cultuur; current programme title: Spaanse en Latijns-Amerikaanse studies)
comparator.academicYear: 2026-2027 current published UvA bachelor curriculum, checked 2026-09-27
comparator.sourceNotes: The current UvA prospectus presents the programme as Spaanse en Latijns-Amerikaanse studies, while the 2026-2027 UvA Study Guide retains the formal programme identity Spaanse Taal en Cultuur, 180 EC, and the overview identifies diploma title BA Spaanse taal en cultuur and RIO code 56810. This is therefore a current presentation-name change within the normalized target, not a different programme. The published full-time curriculum totals 60+60+60=180 EC. Year 1 combines four successive Spanish-proficiency courses with Spanish-speaking-world history and foundations in humanities, linguistics, literature and Spanish sociolinguistics. Year 2 combines two further Spanish-proficiency courses, philosophy of science, Latin American studies, Spanish-language literary study and a compulsory 30-EC semester at a Spanish or Latin American university. Year 3 combines translation and interculturality, advanced Spanish-language literary/cultural and multilingualism study, 30 EC genuine free choice and a 12-EC bachelor thesis written in Spanish. No particular host courses, minor, internship or electives are invented.

programmes.label: Spanish Language and Culture (Spaanse Taal en Cultuur; current programme title: Spaanse en Latijns-Amerikaanse studies) at University of Amsterdam

exception.reason: The defining curriculum requires six successive Spanish-proficiency courses, advanced subject teaching conducted almost entirely in Spanish, Spanish-language literary and sociolinguistic analysis, translation, a compulsory semester in Spain or Latin America, and a bachelor thesis written in Spanish. The current UCR catalogue contains no Spanish-language course and no staged Spanish reading, writing, speaking or translation sequence. A 24-course programme assembled from general literature, communication, psycholinguistics, history and social science would replace the compulsory language-acquisition and Spanish/Latin American disciplinary core rather than provide a defensible closest UCR match. The 30 EC of genuine open choice cannot compensate for the missing 150-EC compulsory core.
exception.curriculumContext: The current full-time curriculum totals exactly 180 EC: 60 EC in year one, 60 EC in year two and 60 EC in year three. It includes six 6-EC Spanish-proficiency courses, Spanish-speaking-world history, linguistics and literature foundations, Spanish-language sociolinguistics and literary study, contemporary Latin American studies, a 30-EC Spanish/Latin American university semester, translation and interculturality, advanced Spanish-language cultural and multilingualism study, 30 EC genuine free choice and a 12-EC thesis written in Spanish. No host-university courses, minor, internship or electives are invented.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 rows of the current enriched UCR course workbook, including course names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, prerequisites, planned availability, disciplines, topics and methods. MCCCOMM112 Dutch is the catalogue's only dedicated modern-language acquisition course and does not provide Spanish. HCBCOGN312 Psycholinguistics studies cognitive and neurobiological language processing; MCCCOMM211 Style & Meaning studies linguistic choices in mainly English-language texts; MCCLITR111 Introduction to Literary Studies, MCCLITR112 Great Literary Works and MCCLITR312 Perspectives on Literary Meaning provide general literary analysis; GOSHIST211 History of Empires, GOSSOCI214 Modern Sociology and the political-science curriculum provide broad historical and social frameworks. These are adjacent methods or contexts, but none teaches Spanish, Spanish-language source analysis, Spanish translation, or a sustained Spain and Latin America regional sequence. The workbook therefore provides no defensible basis for a scheduled 24-course UCR Spanish Language and Culture programme.
